title: Forecast Discipline Ledger: a longitudinal record of agent forecasts and operational errors
description:
Two linked datasets produced by a language-model agent running a daily forecasting process over six financial assets under human supervision. This version is a frozen study window, 2026-08-01 to 2026-10-31 (92 calendar days, 77 forecast days): a row is included only if the forecast was written, its target date fell, and its outcome was observed inside the window.

1. A forecast calibration ledger. On each run the agent writes a point forecast, an 80% interval and a probability of an up-move for each asset at 1-day, 1-week and 1-month horizons, before the outcome is known. Forecasts are sealed, then scored automatically against the realized value and against three baselines (naive, drift, momentum). 1361 forecasts, 1241 resolution rows.

2. An agent error log. Every operational mistake is recorded with structured fields: error class, the mechanism that caught it, who caught it (agent or human), how many days it stayed hidden, and a link to an earlier record where one applies. 146 records; 116 caught by the agent and 30 by the human; detection latency median 1 day, mean 6.0, max 60; 48.6% are flagged as repeats of an earlier record.

Headline results are negative and were pre-registered. In the primary pool (latest protocol version, 1-day and 1-week horizons, 706 rows on 62 forecast days) the agent beats all three baselines at once in 217/706 = 0.307 of rows and on 9 of 58 forecast days. Interval coverage is 0.888 against an 0.80 target. The pooled Brier skill score is positive only because one managed-rate asset rose on every scored row; against each asset's own base rate it is -0.019.

Known limitations. The error log is written by the same agent that made the errors, so errors it never noticed are absent. The routine did not run on 6 of 64 market days, the last 4 of the window among them. Four model versions wrote forecasts in the window.

Anonymization. No amounts, balances, unit counts, price levels, institution, instrument, vendor or person names, market calendar, or free text. Assets appear as A1-A8, models as model_A to model_D, decisions as D1 onward, and country-specific market variables under role labels; global public benchmarks keep their usual names. Accepted residual risk: a fund's return series could in principle be matched against public price series and the instrument identified, which reveals nothing about any person.

analysis/reproduce.py regenerates the reported figures from the CSV files using the standard library only. Earlier versions of this record are running tallies of the same ledger and are superseded by this one.
